root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical evidence is centered on blood and the state of blood issuing, with extensions to making bloody, blood-red coloration, and figurative or conventional uses.
root_idea.development: The family develops from the concrete noun “blood” and the verb “to bleed” to causative, adjectival, color, and specialized applications. Some peripheral Form X usages are explicitly reported as transpositions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The QAC group represents the Quran-attested noun دَم, with ten occurrences.

senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in singular and irregular plural forms, including possessive and definite constructions. Quranic contexts include human or animal blood, blood mentioned in dietary prohibitions, and blood associated with sacrificial animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bleed; to have blood issue from it; to become bloody or smeared with blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive verb describing the issuing of blood or the resulting bloody state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone bleed, causing blood to issue by striking or smiting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make bloody; to smear or defile with blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form II usage, including causing a person or thing to be smeared or defiled with blood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of pasture or herbage, to fatten cattle until they resemble dolls or images.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A marked figurative or transferred usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a way easy; to bring a desired object near.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative constructions involving facilitation or bringing something within reach.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To appear or become apparent to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction خُذْ مَا دَمَّى لَكَ, “take what has appeared to you.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stoop with blood dropping from the head or nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related active participle describes one in this condition. The usage is reported alongside a transposed form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deal gently with a debtor while seeking repayment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage reported as formed by transposition from اِسْتَدَامَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To watch for, wait for, or seek someone’s affection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage reported as formed by transposition from اِسْتَدَامَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dragon’s blood: a red, resinous, inspissated juice, also called the blood of the gazelle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plant-resin term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular herb or leguminous plant with a beautiful blossom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular red plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal name recorded in the lexicon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bleeding; having blood issue from it; bloody or smeared with blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use, distinct from the noun دَم meaning “blood.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: An image or effigy, especially one of ivory, marble, or another decorated material; an idol. Figuratively, a beautiful woman or anything beautiful in respect of whiteness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote an image in general and, by metonymy, a beautiful person or object. In the oath لَا وَالدُّمَى, it is interpreted either as “by the idols” or as referring to blood sacrificed on worship stones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Garments bearing pictures or effigies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural usage of دُمْيَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good fortune, prosperity, or good luck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical item with variant spelling reported in the source tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pertaining or relating to blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective formed from دَم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hectic fever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal Egyptian medical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poor or destitute, literally “having a bleeding lip.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beautiful tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A marked figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A head wound that bleeds but has not yet begun to flow freely with blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical description of a wound; one that flows with blood is distinguished by another term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blood-red, dark red, or intensely red; of a horse, intensely sorrel or red like blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to garments, colors, horses, and similar objects; the color may include a blackish cast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow marked or stained with blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression with several traditional explanations, all involving an arrow associated with blood or having been shot in combat.
